notes: Procedural skill. Eval prompts produce a test file / written procedure (no real-engine model spend needed to grade). Baseline is somewhat non-blind because the skill's files live in the repo working tree; treat the lift as understated.

evals.name: write-cancel-e2e
evals.prompt: I just changed `codex wait` so a cancelled job exits 2. Write an end-to-end test for the codex plugin that proves this, and make sure the test would actually fail on the old code.
evals.expected_output: A hermetic e2e test that drives the real codex-companion.mjs as a subprocess in an isolated workspace, seeds a terminal cancelled job via the plugin's state writers, asserts exit code 2, and is shown to be a true regression (fails on pre-fix code).

assertions.text: drives the real codex-companion.mjs via spawnSync (not in-process)
seeds a cancelled job directly (terminal seed; no pid juggling needed)
shows non-vacuity: would fail on old code (revert-the-line or base worktree)

evals.name: verify-two-layer
evals.prompt: I refactored the fleet status board. How do I verify it end-to-end against the real engines, and how is that different from just running the test suite?
evals.expected_output: A procedure that distinguishes the hermetic suite (npm run test:e2e, fake engines) from the real-engine smoke (manual gate), checks readiness via fleet-doctor first, runs the bundled real-engine-smoke.mjs, and notes the cost/manual-gate caveat.

assertions.text: distinguishes hermetic (fake) layer from real-engine layer
checks readiness via fleet-doctor --json before any real run
notes the real layer is a manual gate that costs real model tokens
